Senses.Explanation: A fly-whisk is a handle bearing a tuft used for brushing away flies or dust. In Chan records it is also a teaching-seat implement and an emblem of the presiding teacher's authority, not merely a duster. Asked what he uses to show people, Baizhang Huaihai raises the whisk. Xishan Heshang answers the question of the patriarch's coming from the West by showing it; Xingkong Guan draws a stroke with it to cut off preceding entanglements; Beijian Jujian strikes the Chan seat with it; and Sanyi Yu mimes playing a flute with it. In another encounter Donglin Changzong strikes Wanshan Shaoci across the mouth with the whisk; Wanshan seizes it and bows. Xueguan Zhiyin explicitly contrasts the two implements: “the staff establishes; the fly-whisk sweeps away,” while calling them equal in weight. Its institutional force is equally explicit. Chuiwan Guangzhen says that he has tested Yinran and “specially bestows one fly-whisk” so Yinran may continue Dahui's line. Jifei Ruyi transmits a whisk to Fayun, who accepts it and states how he will raise it. To brush or whisk away (拂), plus a noun suffix (子): a fly-whisk. The headword is frequent across the allowlisted corpus. Miyun Yuanwu gives a fixed naming test: “call it a whisk and you offend; do not call it a whisk and you turn your back on it.” Sanping Yizhong pairs the impossible “tortoise-hair whisk” with a “rabbit-horn staff.” Raising, striking, seizing, drawing, miming, showing, and transmitting all involve the same physical implement; its Zen bend lies in who wields, contests, or bestows it and where it acts.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide object sense: the fly-whisk as teaching-seat implement and emblem of authority. The curated passages include bestowal and receipt as a lineage credential, a nonverbal interview answer, direct striking and seizure, the text's staff/whisk functional contrast, drawing, and representational mime as well as raising, naming, the impossible variant, the whisk-tip, and striking the seat. These deployments do not create separate object senses.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Transmission Lamp Jade-Flower Collection (傳燈玉英集（殘卷）), in Huangbo Xiyun's section, records Baizhang Huaihai raising the whisk after Huangbo asks what teaching Baizhang uses to show people. The stored occurrence is trimmed to Baizhang's exact action; Huangbo is the questioner outside it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 握拂子云：『喚作拂子則觸，不喚作拂子則背，不得拈起、不得放下、不得下語、不得無語
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wufeng Ruxue, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dawei Wufeng Xue (大溈五峰學禪師語錄), explicitly recalls his own teacher Miyun Yuanwu gripping the whisk and stating the naming test. The explicit speaker shift to ‘my teacher’ overrides title-first attribution; MasterName is Miyun Yuanwu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「大德龜毛拂子、兔角柱杖藏著何處？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), in Sanping Yizhong's section, records Sanping Yizhong asking where the impossible tortoise-hair whisk and rabbit-horn staff are stored. The whole exchange identifies the section teacher as the speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 遂舉拂子云大眾從上許多賢聖如今緫在山僧拂子頭上各各坐大蓮華
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Foyan Qingyuan, in his section of Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), lifts the whisk during a hall address and says that the sages of old now sit on his whisk-tip.

Occurrences.Kwic: 以拂子擊禪床云當機覿面提覿面當機疾
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Beijian Jujian, in the Beijian record embedded in Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), strikes the Chan seat with the whisk during his own Jingci hall address. The surrounding unit contains no guest-speaker or quoted-case shift.

Occurrences.Kwic: 老僧勘驗有在，特付拂子一枝，以續大慧之裔云。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Chuiwan Guangzhen, in the entrustment to Yinran in his Recorded Sayings (聚雲吹萬真禪師語錄), says that his testing has grounds and specially bestows one fly-whisk so Yinran may continue Dahui's line. The complete entrustment unit keeps Chuiwan as speaker throughout.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲接拂子曰：「直向佛祖斫額不及處提時，當報不報之恩。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Record of Chan Master Jifei (即非禪師全錄) records Jifei Ruyi transmitting a whisk to his disciple Fayun; Fayun then accepts it and states how he will raise it. MasterName identifies Fayun's exact turn, not the record owner. The source supplies only the name Fayun for this recipient.

Occurrences.Kwic: 以拂子畫一畫，曰：前來葛藤，一時劃斷。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), in Xingkong Guan's section, records Xingkong Guan drawing one stroke with the fly-whisk and saying that the preceding entanglements are cut off at once.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問。三乘十二分教則不問。如何是祖師西來的的意。師舉拂子示之。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), in the section titled ‘Suzhou Xishan Heshang,’ records Xishan Heshang raising and showing the fly-whisk when asked for the exact meaning of the patriarch's coming from the West. The source gives no personal name.

Occurrences.Kwic: 以拂子作品笛勢云：「咿唔。」遂下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Sanyi Yu, in his own hall address in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanyi Yu (三宜盂禪師語錄), uses the fly-whisk to mime playing a flute, vocalizes, and steps down. The full address contains no speaker shift.

The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), in Wanshan Shaoci's biography, records his teacher Donglin Changzong, called Zhaojue in the exchange, striking Wanshan across the mouth with the fly-whisk. This trimmed occurrence contains Donglin's exact action only.

The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), in Wanshan Shaoci's biography, records Wanshan seizing the fly-whisk from Donglin Changzong and bowing. This separate occurrence assigns Wanshan's exact action to Wanshan, not to his teacher. Wanshan Shaoci is not yet on the roster.
